minor.issue: App correctly sets Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 (verified via localhost:8001), but Cloudflare/K8s ingress rewrites the response header to 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' on the public URL. This nullifies browser + CDN caching for OG images. Not fixable in app code — infrastructure-level.

integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL: react-helmet-async only APPENDS meta tags without removing duplicates. index.html declares default og:title, og:description, og:type, og:site_name, twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:description and 2× <meta name=description>. When PublicBriefingPage's <Helmet> re-declares them, the DOM ends up with duplicates (2 og:title, 2 og:description, 2 og:type, 2 og:site_name, 3 description). Social scrapers typically read the FIRST occurrence, so previews on Facebook/Twitter/LinkedIn will show the default 'Lume Veritas — le notizie che i giornali trascurano' and the generic description instead of the article headline and summary. Fix: remove the default og:*/twitter:*/description meta tags from /app/frontend/public/index.html (keep only <title> and neutral <meta name=description>), so Helmet is the sole owner of these tags on /s/:id and other pages fall back to whatever remains. Alternatively, keep index.html defaults but change key strategy — however react-helmet-async fundamentally cannot manage pre-existing head elements that weren't rendered by React.

action_items: HIGH PRIORITY — Fix duplicate meta tags on /s/:id: remove default og:title, og:description, og:type, og:site_name, twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:description and the 'A product of emergent.sh' <meta name=description> from /app/frontend/public/index.html so that <Helmet> in PublicBriefingPage.jsx is the sole authority. Keep <title>, <meta name=viewport>, <link rel=stylesheet> etc. Verify by re-running the Playwright script and asserting exactly ONE <meta property='og:title'> in document.head with content === item.headline.
(Info) app-level Cache-Control on /api/og/{id}.png is correct (verified via localhost); the ingress override to no-store is infrastructure-side and out of scope for the app.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 899 lines — exceeds the 700-line soft cap. Strongly recommend splitting: routers/{auth,news,rss,tts,digest,public,og}.py, services/{llm,tts,email}.py, jobs/scheduler.py, models.py, config.py.

In public_briefing, the view increment `db.briefings.update_one({...}, {'$inc': {'views': 1}})` runs AFTER an optional deep_dive() call and then the code manually adds 1 to doc['views']. Because deep_dive() reads and updates the same doc, a race between concurrent viewers can produce off-by-one under load. Consider using MongoDB $inc atomically and reading back the updated document via return_document=AFTER (motor supports find_one_and_update).

The OG image fallback path (`if not doc: png = _render_og_image('LUME VERITAS', ...)`) is nice, but there is no ETag/Last-Modified header — combined with the ingress overriding Cache-Control, every OG image request re-renders (~200ms Pillow work). Add ETag hashing (e.g., hash of topic+headline) so clients (and any downstream cache that respects ETag despite Cache-Control) can 304.

PublicBriefingPage.jsx: `viewsLabel` uses `item.views || 1` as fallback — this hides a zero-views state (a doc that has never been fetched before shows 1, not 0). Since GET /public/{id} increments views before returning, the first render will always be >=1, but if the endpoint were ever called without increment (e.g., preview), it would still show 1.

PublicBriefingPage.jsx: no dependency on `lang` in the ogImage URL — server renders OG image with headline in the language stored on the doc, but on shareUrl language switching there is no signal. Minor since OG images are meant to be language-agnostic snapshots.

index.html duplicates <meta name='description'> twice (line 7 'A product of emergent.sh' and line 25 'Lume Veritas: notizie...') even before Helmet adds a third — pre-existing bug independent of iter 4.

OG rendering uses `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` for the date shown on the image instead of `doc.generated_at` — so the OG image ALWAYS shows today's date, not the article's publication date. Consider using generated_at.

rca of the issue: Meta tag duplication RCA: react-helmet-async manages ONLY the tags it renders. It has no mechanism to remove pre-existing <meta> tags that were in the initial HTML (index.html). When PublicBriefingPage's <Helmet> renders <meta property='og:title'>, the library adds a new element to <head>, but the original <meta property='og:title' content='Lume Veritas — le notizie...' /> from index.html line 28 remains. Result: 2 elements with property=og:title in <head>. Social scrapers (og:image debugger, Facebook Sharing Debugger, Twitter Card Validator) typically pick the FIRST occurrence they encounter, so they render the STATIC default title/description instead of the dynamic article-specific values. Reproduction: navigate to any /s/<id>, run in DevTools console: `document.head.querySelectorAll('meta[property="og:title"]')` — length is 2. Mitigation: strip default og:*/twitter:*/description meta tags from /app/frontend/public/index.html so Helmet becomes the single source of truth for these tags.
